basic_information.name: turbopuffer
basic_information.creator: turbopuffer Inc., co-founded by Simon Horup Eskildsen (CEO, ex-Principal Engineer/Director at Shopify) and Justine Li (CTO, ex-Infrastructure Engineer at Shopify). Headquartered in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada with presence in Vancouver and New York City.
basic_information.description: turbopuffer is a serverless vector and full-text search engine built from first principles on object storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob). It represents a fundamentally different approach to vector databases by being the first completely object-storage-native database, achieving up to 95% cost reduction compared to memory-based solutions like Pinecone while maintaining competitive query latency through intelligent tiered caching. turbopuffer leverages three technological advances: NVMe SSDs that are only 4-5x slower than memory but 100x cheaper than DRAM, S3's strong consistency guarantees (introduced 2020), and S3's compare-and-swap functionality (launched December 2023). It supports both vector similarity search and BM25 full-text search with hybrid search capabilities. In production, turbopuffer handles 2.5T+ documents, 10M+ writes/s, and 10k+ queries/s for customers including Cursor, Notion, Anthropic, and Atlassian.
basic_information.release_date: Founded 2023; first version built by Simon Eskildsen over summer 2023; public launch October 4, 2023; ANN v3 (100B-vector scale) announced 2025
basic_information.license: Proprietary (fully managed SaaS). No open-source server component. Client SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Ruby, Go, Java) are open-source on GitHub.
basic_information.github_stars: Not applicable for core product (closed-source). Python client (turbopuffer/turbopuffer-python) on GitHub. Various official client SDKs across Python, TypeScript, Ruby, Go, Java maintained under the turbopuffer GitHub organization.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Serverless, object-storage-native, distributed. Three-tier storage hierarchy that automatically moves data based on access patterns: (1) Object Storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) as the sole stateful dependency at ~$0.02/GB for cold storage with 200-500ms query latency, (2) NVMe SSD Cache at ~$0.10/GB for warm storage with queries in tens of milliseconds, (3) Memory for hot data. Data inflates from object storage to disk to RAM as needed. Compute is fully separated from state — the only stateful dependency is object storage. This enables true serverless scaling with no pre-provisioned infrastructure.
technical_architecture.language: Polyglot tech stack. The turbopuffer GitHub organization maintains repositories in Rust, Go, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, and Java. The core engine implementation language is not publicly disclosed but evidence points to Rust and Go. Official client SDKs in Python (v0.5+, generated with Stainless, async support via httpx), TypeScript, Ruby, Go, and Java. Benchmarking tool (tpuf-benchmark) written in Go.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports standard embedding dimensions. Documented benchmarks use 768-dimensional vectors (e.g., 1M vectors at 768 dimensions = 3GB). Maximum supported dimensions not publicly documented, but compatible with all major embedding model outputs. [uncertain]
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Vector indexes based on SPFresh, a centroid-based approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) index. A centroid-based index minimizes roundtrips and write-amplification compared to graph-based indexes (HNSW, DiskANN), making it ideal for object storage. The fast index locates the nearest centroids to the query vector, then fetches relevant data. Additionally supports an inverted BM25 index for keyword/full-text search. During vector search, turbopuffer first evaluates on quantized vectors, uses error bounds to determine all vectors that could be in the true top-k, fetches their full-precision vectors, and reranks — less than 1% of vectors need reranking, preserving recall. ANN v3 architecture scales to 100B+ vectors at thousands of QPS with 200ms p99 latency.
technical_architecture.scalability: Demonstrated at extreme scale: 2.5T+ documents, 100B+ vectors (Cursor), 10B+ vectors (Notion), 10M+ writes/s, 10k+ queries/s in production. Multi-tenant architecture supports millions of namespaces (Cursor: 10M+ namespaces, Notion: 1M+ namespaces). Horizontal scaling is handled automatically. No pre-provisioned capacity needed — serverless model scales compute on demand.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Cloud-managed serverless only. Available on AWS (S3), GCP (GCS), and Azure (Blob Storage). No self-hosted option. No Docker/Kubernetes deployment. Accessible via HTTP API with official SDKs. Enterprise plan available with additional features (CMEK, dedicated support).

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector similarity search (ANN via SPFresh centroid-based index), sparse keyword search (BM25 inverted index), and hybrid search combining both. Supports metadata filtering with fast vector similarity search and advanced filtering capabilities. Hybrid search enables robust candidate set generation for downstream refinement. Quantized vector search with automatic full-precision reranking for recall preservation.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: No built-in chunking capabilities. turbopuffer is a vector/search database, not a document processing pipeline. Chunking is delegated to upstream tools and orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, custom pipelines). Users are responsible for chunking documents before upserting vectors.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in internal reranking during vector search: turbopuffer evaluates on quantized vectors first, then fetches and reranks full-precision vectors for candidates that could be in the true top-k (typically less than 1% of vectors). For external reranking, turbopuffer integrates with third-party rerankers. A documented integration example uses turbopuffer + ZeroEntropy for hybrid search with reranking. Compatible with cross-encoder rerankers via LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: turbopuffer stores vectors from any modality — text, image, audio, or video embeddings can all be indexed as vectors. However, there are no built-in multimodal embedding or processing capabilities. Users bring their own multimodal embeddings (e.g., CLIP, ImageBind) and store the resulting vectors in turbopuffer.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native knowledge graph or GraphRAG capabilities. turbopuffer is a vector and full-text search engine. Graph-enhanced retrieval would require combining turbopuffer with a graph database or using frameworks that support GraphRAG with turbopuffer as the vector backend.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: No built-in source attribution or citation generation. Metadata associated with vectors (source document, page, chunk ID) can be stored and returned alongside search results to enable citation at the application layer. Grounding verification is the developer's responsibility.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: No built-in context window management. turbopuffer returns search results; fitting those results into LLM context windows is handled by the application or orchestration framework. The hybrid search capability (dense + BM25) helps generate higher-quality candidate sets, reducing the number of irrelevant chunks that consume context window space.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Cold queries (first query, data on object storage): p50=343ms for 1M documents, p90=444ms for 768-dim vectors. Warm/cached queries: p50=8ms, p90=10ms, p99=35ms for 1M documents. At 100B+ vector scale (ANN v3): p99=200ms at thousands of QPS. Linear (250M+ documents): 13ms p50 latency. Consistent reads have a ~10ms latency floor due to object storage checks.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Production workloads: 10M+ writes/s, 10k+ queries/s. ANN v3 architecture sustains thousands of QPS at 100B-vector scale. Cursor handles 10GB/s write peaks; Notion handles 1GB/s write peaks.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: turbopuffer automatically samples 1% of all queries in production to measure the accuracy of the vector index (continuous recall measurement). The quantized-then-rerank approach ensures high recall by fetching full-precision vectors for all candidates that could be in the true top-k based on error bounds. Exact recall@k numbers not publicly published. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Official benchmarks on turbopuffer.com/docs/benchmark. At 1M 768-dim vectors: cold p50=343ms, warm p50=8ms. ANN v3: 200ms p99 at 100B vectors at thousands of QPS. Not included in standard open ANN-Benchmarks suite (closed-source). Third-party comparisons (ZenML, Liveblocks) position turbopuffer as cost-optimized with competitive warm latency but higher cold-start latency than in-memory alternatives. [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: LangChain integration via langchain-turbopuffer package (unofficial/community binding, available on PyPI). LlamaIndex: no dedicated turbopuffer integration found, but can integrate via LangChain bridge or custom vector store. Mastra framework has a documented turbopuffer vector store reference. Compatible with general RAG orchestration via the HTTP API and official SDKs.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Compatible with all embedding models and LLM providers — turbopuffer stores vectors from any model. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Cohere, and any open-source embedding model. No built-in embedding generation — users generate embeddings externally and store them in turbopuffer.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: No official turbopuffer MCP server found in search results. Integration with Claude and MCP-compatible tools is possible through framework-level connectors but no dedicated MCP server is documented. [uncertain]
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: No native first-party data source connectors (S3, Confluence, Notion, etc.). Data ingestion is handled via the HTTP API and official SDKs. Connector functionality is delegated to orchestration frameworks (LangChain document loaders, LlamaIndex data connectors) or custom pipelines. turbopuffer itself uses S3/GCS/Azure Blob as its storage backend, not as a data source connector.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: No specific turbopuffer observability integrations documented in search results. Monitoring and tracing would be handled at the application/framework layer using tools like LangSmith, Langfuse, or Arize Phoenix via LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations. turbopuffer likely provides basic usage metrics and dashboards for customers. [uncertain]

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Usage-based serverless pricing: pay for storage, writes, and queries. No pre-provisioned capacity. Pricing updated December 2025 with cheaper rates for large namespaces and lower cost for simpler queries. Storage leverages object storage at ~$0.02/GB (compared to ~$0.60/GB for traditional SSD-based databases). Enterprise plan available with CMEK and dedicated support. Interactive pricing calculator at turbopuffer.com/pricing.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: No free tier currently available. turbopuffer has minimum spend requirements, which the team describes as ensuring a high-quality support experience rather than infrastructure limitations. Plans to lower minimum spend and eventually offer a free tier over time.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Object storage: ~$0.02/GB. SSD cache: ~$0.10/GB. For standard pricing tests, cost comes in under $10/month with a minimum spend of $64/month. Cursor achieved 95% cost reduction compared to their previous vector DB solution. Notion saves millions annually. Linear achieved 70% cost reduction. turbopuffer claims 10x-100x cheaper than traditional in-memory vector databases. At very large scale (100B+ vectors, tens of petabytes), the object-storage-first architecture provides dramatic cost advantages over memory-based alternatives.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: TCO includes: turbopuffer usage fees (storage + writes + queries) + external embedding generation costs + LLM inference costs + orchestration framework costs. The serverless model eliminates infrastructure management overhead — no cluster management, capacity planning, or scaling decisions. Major TCO advantage comes from the storage tier: object storage at $0.02/GB vs DRAM at $2+/GB (100x difference) or SSD at $0.60/GB (30x difference). For large-scale workloads (1B+ vectors), turbopuffer's cost advantage is most pronounced. The minimum spend requirement ($64/month) means it is less suited for very small hobby projects compared to free-tier alternatives.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Emerging/challenger with rapid growth trajectory. turbopuffer is carving a distinctive niche as the object-storage-native alternative to established vector databases. Still smaller than Pinecone, Weaviate, or Milvus/Zilliz in overall market share, but rapidly gaining enterprise customers due to dramatic cost savings. ARR grew to 'tens of millions' in 2025 with 10x revenue growth. The company has gained attention from the AI infrastructure community as a fundamentally new approach to vector search economics.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Cursor (AI code editor — 95% cost reduction, 100B+ vectors, 10GB/s write peaks, 10M+ namespaces), Notion (AI workspace — saves millions annually, 10B+ vectors, 1GB/s write peaks, 1M+ namespaces), Anthropic (AI safety/LLM company), Atlassian (enterprise software), Linear (project management — 70% cost reduction, 250M+ documents, 13ms p50, 1.5M+ namespaces), Superhuman (email — intelligent search and organization), Suno (AI music — radio feature), New Computer/Dot (AI companion — memory system), TELUS (Canadian telecommunications — second major enterprise customer, early 2024).
adoption_and_market.community_size: 22 employees as of late 2025 (headcount grew 5x in 2025). No public Discord or Slack community documented. Active on X/Twitter (@turbopuffer). LinkedIn presence. GitHub organization (github.com/turbopuffer) maintains multiple client SDK repositories. Community engagement primarily through blog posts, technical talks, and direct customer relationships rather than open-source community.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Investors include Thrive Capital, Lachy Groom (former head of Stripe Issuing, co-founder of Physical Intelligence), Redpoint Ventures, and AWS (GovTech Accelerator, EdStart). Exact funding amounts and valuation not publicly disclosed. Thrive Capital's investment is described as one of their most recent first-time investments. Revenue: ARR in the 'tens of millions' as of 2025, with 10x revenue growth year-over-year. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Pinecone (fully managed, larger market share, more integrations, higher cost), Qdrant (open-source, Rust-based, strong metadata filtering, self-hostable), Weaviate (open-source, GraphQL, knowledge graph features), Milvus/Zilliz (open-source, extreme scale, lowest raw latency), Chroma (lightweight, developer-friendly). Key differentiators for turbopuffer: (1) Object-storage-first architecture — fundamentally different cost structure (10-100x cheaper storage), (2) Serverless with zero pre-provisioned infrastructure, (3) Built-in hybrid search (vector + BM25), (4) Proven at extreme scale (100B+ vectors, trillions of documents), (5) Founded by Shopify infrastructure veterans who scaled systems from 1k to 1M RPS. turbopuffer is proprietary like Pinecone, not open-source like Qdrant/Weaviate/Milvus.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best suited for: (1) Growth-stage startups with large vector workloads where cost matters — if you have 100M+ vectors and are spending significantly on Pinecone or self-hosted solutions, turbopuffer can reduce costs by 70-95%. (2) AI-native companies building code search, knowledge management, or search-heavy products (following the Cursor/Notion pattern). (3) Teams that want serverless simplicity without managing infrastructure. Less suited for: (1) Very early-stage startups or hobby projects — the minimum spend ($64/month) and lack of a free tier means Pinecone (free starter) or Chroma (local) are better for POCs. (2) Teams requiring extensive ecosystem integrations — turbopuffer has fewer framework integrations than Pinecone or Qdrant. (3) Teams needing open-source or self-hosted deployment for compliance reasons. Team size consideration: turbopuffer is ideal for teams of any size that have large-scale vector workloads but want to minimize infrastructure engineering effort.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Buy (use turbopuffer managed) when: you have large vector datasets (100M+ vectors), cost reduction is a priority, you want serverless simplicity, and your use case fits vector + BM25 search. Consider alternatives when: you need a free tier for prototyping (use Pinecone Starter or Chroma), you need extensive GraphRAG or knowledge graph features (use Weaviate or Neo4j), you need self-hosted deployment for data sovereignty (use Qdrant or Milvus), or you need the broadest possible ecosystem integration (use Pinecone). There is no self-hosted option for turbopuffer — it is fully managed SaaS only.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 1-3 days (sign up, integrate SDK, upsert vectors, query). Production deployment: 1-2 weeks for a basic pipeline. The serverless architecture eliminates infrastructure setup time. Migration from existing vector DBs: Cursor migrated their entire workload within one week (CEO Simon flew to SF and worked directly with the team). Enterprise deployment with security review: 2-4 weeks depending on compliance requirements.
key_lessons: Object storage economics are a paradigm shift for vector databases — storing vectors at $0.02/GB instead of $2+/GB (DRAM) or $0.60/GB (SSD) changes the unit economics of AI products fundamentally. This matters most at scale (100M+ vectors).

Cold-start latency is the tradeoff — turbopuffer's first query to a namespace is slow (200-500ms) but subsequent cached queries are fast (8ms p50). Design your application to handle or mask cold starts (pre-warming, background queries, graceful degradation).

Hybrid search (vector + BM25) in a single database simplifies architecture — instead of running separate vector and keyword search systems, turbopuffer handles both. This reduces operational complexity and improves retrieval quality for RAG.

The 'white-glove' approach works for infrastructure startups — turbopuffer's CEO flew to customers, did hands-on migrations, and ensured success. This high-touch model built trust with Cursor, Notion, and others despite being a young company.

Consider total cost of ownership, not just per-query price — turbopuffer may not have a free tier, but for workloads at scale, the 70-95% cost reduction (as demonstrated by Cursor, Notion, Linear) dwarfs the minimum monthly spend.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: No — turbopuffer does not provide a visual/no-code builder for RAG pipelines. It is a developer-focused API-first product. Integration requires writing code using the official SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Ruby, Go, Java) or HTTP API.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy decisions for vector infrastructure, cost analysis of managed vs self-hosted) and Session 4 (AI business models — unit economics of object-storage-first architecture, scaling economics). Also relevant to Session 1 as a case study of AI infrastructure innovation by ex-Shopify engineers.

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from turbopuffer's official website, blog posts, and documentation; BetaKit for funding and company details; PMF.show for founder interviews and customer case studies; CBInsights, Crunchbase, and Tracxn for company profiles; Medium and Substack for technical analyses; ZenML and Liveblocks for third-party comparisons.
confidence.cross_reference: Customer claims (Cursor 95% cost reduction, Notion millions saved, Linear 70% cost reduction) confirmed across multiple sources including turbopuffer's customer page, BetaKit, and PMF.show. Founding date (2023) and founders confirmed across Crunchbase, CBInsights, Tracxn, and press. Architecture details (SPFresh, object storage tiers) confirmed across official docs, Jason Liu's technical analysis, and Software Engineering Daily podcast. Revenue growth (10x in 2025, ARR in tens of millions) confirmed via LinkedIn post and BetaKit. Investor list (Thrive Capital, Lachy Groom, Redpoint) confirmed across Crunchbase and BetaKit.
confidence.caveats: Exact funding amounts and valuation are undisclosed. Specific per-query and per-write pricing details require visiting the interactive pricing calculator (turbopuffer.com/pricing) — exact unit prices not available in search results. Implementation language of the core engine is not publicly confirmed (likely Rust/Go based on GitHub repos). Maximum supported embedding dimensions not documented. MCP integration status and observability integrations are uncertain. The company is young (founded 2023) and rapidly evolving — features, pricing, and benchmarks may change frequently. Cold-start latency (200-500ms) is a genuine architectural tradeoff that may not suit latency-sensitive applications without caching strategies.
confidence.security_posture: SOC 2 Type 2 certified (audits of design and operational effectiveness of security and availability controls). SOC 2 report and penetration test available via Trust Center. Customer Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) available on Enterprise plan — customers can encrypt data using their own KMS/EKM keys. Data encrypted at rest in object storage. Known vector DB attack surfaces (embedding inversion, knowledge base poisoning) are industry-wide concerns. turbopuffer mitigates with encryption, access controls, and enterprise-grade compliance.
